diagnosis.root_cause: The Python script `collect_test_data.py` failed when attempting to fetch GitHub Actions runs via the GitHub REST API. The API returned a 500 Internal Server Error from the endpoint `https://api.github.com/repos/tharindra0622-sys/gha-demo/actions/runs?status=completed&per_page=50&page=1`. The Log Analyst identified the exact error: "requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 500 Server Error: Internal Server Error for url: https://api.github.com/repos/tharindra0622-sys/gha-demo/actions/runs?status=completed&per_page=50&page=1". This is an upstream infrastructure issue with GitHub's API, not a code defect. The External Analyst found multiple community reports (Reddit and GitHub discussions) confirming that the GitHub Actions REST API `/actions/runs` endpoint intermittently returns 500 errors, indicating this is a known transient issue with GitHub's infrastructure. The History Analyst found five similar issues (#452, #279, #250, #221, #448) all showing the same pattern of 500 Server Errors from the GitHub API. The Config & Change Analyst found no configuration problems or relevant recent code changes.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff in the `collect_test_data.py` script when calling the GitHub API. Since this is a known intermittent GitHub API issue (confirmed by multiple community reports and historical occurrences in issues #452, #279, #250, #221, #448), the script should retry failed requests 3-5 times with increasing delays (e.g., 2s, 4s, 8s) before failing. Additionally, consider adding better error handling to distinguish between transient 5xx errors (which should be retried) and permanent 4xx errors (which should fail immediately). Re-run the workflow once to see if the issue has resolved itself.
